findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether any converted curl call reads a body from stdin. If so, have curl_auth pass the config on a separate fd (e.g. `curl -K /dev/fd/3 "$@" 3< <(printf ...)`) so stdin stays free, and add a helper test that a stdin body and the auth header both arrive.
evidence: "`curl_auth <user> <pw> <curl args>`: escapes `\` and `"`, then `printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' | curl -K - "$@"`"
"every `curl -u` becomes `curl_auth`"
No mention of how callers that pipe a JSON body to curl are handled.
findings.finding: `curl_auth` makes curl read its config from stdin (`printf ... | curl -K - "$@"`), but the plan says *every* `curl -u` in the five scripts becomes `curl_auth`. Any existing call that already streams its request body or upload from stdin (`-d @-`, `--data-binary @-`, `-T -`, or a heredoc or pipe feeding curl) cannot also read config from stdin. The plan neither rules such calls out nor specifies an alternative channel.
findings.location: Approach steps 1 and 3 (curl_auth; 'every `curl -u` becomes `curl_auth`')
scenarios: A Gerrit REST POST in reviewbot-e2e.sh that sends JSON via `--data @-`: the body is lost (or parsed as curl config) once wrapped in curl_auth.
A caller passing `-K` itself for other options.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement curl_auth as `curl -K /dev/fd/3 "$@" 3< <(printf 'user = "%s:%s"\n' "$u" "$p")`. printf remains a builtin, only `/dev/fd/3` appears in argv, and caller stdin is untouched. Then update the inventory stub to read the config from the passed `-K` path instead of draining stdin.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify on 3.14.1 which token id `--generate-http-password` creates. Either make the delete target that id or switch to `--delete-token <id>` + `--generate-token <id>` with the same explicit id, and state why the chosen command beats the alternative.
evidence: Plan: "for new and existing accounts it deletes the `default` token (as today) and runs `gerrit set-account <bot> --generate-http-password`"
service-user.sh:53-54: '# Replace Gerrit's default HTTP token. Setting a second default fails.' followed by `--delete-token default 2>/dev/null || true`, which swallows errors silently.

Gerrit REST docs: the Set/Generate HTTP Password endpoint is an alias that 'Sets/Generates an authentication token with id `legacy`'; 'The token-id must be unique among other token-ids used by the account.'
Gerrit cmd-set-account docs now list `[--generate-token <TOKEN-ID>]` and `[--delete-token <TOKEN-ID>]`. The plan does not mention or reject this native option.
findings.finding: Token-id assumption for rotation is unverified. The plan deletes the `default` token and then generates a new one through the deprecated HTTP-password path. Gerrit's current docs say that path 'Sets/Generates an authentication token with id `legacy`', and token ids must be unique per account. If the SSH `--generate-http-password` writes `legacy` rather than `default`, then `--delete-token default` (whose error the script ignores with `|| true`) revokes nothing. The next rotation could then fail on the duplicate `legacy` id or leave the old bot token valid. The plan does not weigh the native, non-deprecated `--generate-token <TOKEN-ID>` option, which would pair explicitly with `--delete-token <TOKEN-ID>`.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (`infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` create/rotate path); AC 1
scenarios: The first rotation after the fix generates id `legacy` while the old `default` token stays valid, so the leaked old token is not revoked.
The second rotation: deleting `default` is a no-op, and generating `legacy` again fails as a duplicate or adds yet another live token.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the native token API with one explicit id: `$GERRIT_SSH gerrit set-account "$BOT_USER" --delete-token default` (tolerate only a 'not found' error), then `$GERRIT_SSH gerrit set-account "$BOT_USER" --generate-token default`, and capture stdout. Confirm on 3.14.1 that afterwards only the new `default` token authenticates, and add that as a measured fact in the plan.

Lines 87-96 `git add webhooks.config` ... `git push -q origin HEAD:refs/meta/config`
findings.finding: The plan keeps the legacy `__BOT_TOKEN__` substitution and tests that 'the render contains it'. For any older template that still has the placeholder, the script then commits and pushes the bot token in plaintext to refs/meta/config, where it stays in git history and is readable by anyone with refs/meta/config read access. The committed template no longer has the placeholder (the only repo hits are the script's own comment and awk line), so keeping this path only preserves a way to put a plaintext secret on a committed path.
findings.location: Approach step 2 ('The template render becomes a bash `while read` loop with `${line//__BOT_TOKEN__/$TOKEN}`'); Testing ('template copy with `__BOT_TOKEN__` ... the render contains it')

findings.suggested_fix: Before any Gerrit call, add `if grep -q __BOT_TOKEN__ "${SCRIPT_DIR}/webhooks.config"; then echo 'service-user: template embeds the token; refusing' >&2; exit 1; fi` and copy the template unchanged instead of rendering it. grep's argv holds only the placeholder, not the secret.

Plan: "for new and existing accounts it deletes the `default` token (as today) and runs `gerrit set-account <bot> --generate-http-password`". Neither the resulting token id nor its lifetime is stated.
Evidence class: Unverified. In the token model (3.13+), how the generate path maps to token ids and lifetimes has not been probed for this image.
findings.finding: Rotation correctness depends on the token Gerrit generates replacing the old credential. The plan deletes the `default` token and then calls `--generate-http-password`, but never confirms which token id 3.14.1 gives the generated credential, or whether it gets an expiry (e.g. a configured maximum auth-token lifetime). If the generated token gets another id, or the delete is silenced and fails, tokens pile up and the old one stays valid. If it expires, the bot loses auth later without warning.
findings.location: Approach step 2; Acceptance Criteria item 1
scenarios: The generated token is stored under a new id while 'default' (the old token) was not removed because the silenced delete failed. The compromised or retired token stays valid after the 'rotation'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Probe `gerrit set-account --generate-http-password` against a throwaway container built from `infra/compose/Dockerfile.gerrit`: record the exact stdout format and which token id it writes, confirm only one token exists after two rotations and the previous one is rejected, then pin the stub output to the recorded format.

findings.finding: The new rotation path rests on an unmeasured claim about Gerrit's output and behaviour. The plan asserts that Gerrit 3.14.1 answers `set-account <bot> --generate-http-password` on stdout with `New password: <pw>`. It also implicitly assumes the generated credential replaces the `default` token the script just deleted. Unlike the curl and aws claims, neither is measured. All service-user.sh tests use an argv-recording `ssh` stub that will simply emit the assumed format, and the script is never run. If the real prefix or format differs, every rotation exits 1. If the generated credential lands under a different token id, earlier generated tokens stay valid after rotation (the rotation would not revoke the old secret).

findings.suggested_fix: Add a Testing bullet: bring up the Gerrit 3.14.1 image locally and run `ssh -p 29418 admin@localhost gerrit set-account test-bot --generate-http-password` twice, deleting `default` before each as the script does. Capture stdout verbatim and list the account's tokens via REST after each run. Assert the first password returns 401 after the second rotation. Use the captured output as the ssh stub's fixture.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the service-user.sh ordering and failure contract: preflight aws/ssh access before deleting `default`, generate, validate, then SSM put and render. On any failure after generation, emit a non-secret error that names the recovery (re-run, or restore via a named runbook step), and add a stub test for the aws-failure-after-generation path.
evidence: "deletes the `default` token (as today) and runs `gerrit set-account <bot> --generate-http-password` ... exits 1 without printing unless the value is non-empty and only `[A-Za-z0-9+/=._~-]`"
No step ordering or failure handling is stated for `aws ssm put-parameter` or the template render after server-side generation.
No rollback/back-out plan is stated for a failed rotation.
findings.finding: The rotation flow has no stated ordering or recovery for partial failure. The script deletes the `default` token and generates a new one on the server first. Only afterwards does it validate the output, write SSM and render the template. If validation fails (exit 1 'without printing'), the aws call fails, or the render fails, Gerrit holds a new credential that is stored nowhere. The old token is already deleted and the new value is deliberately discarded, so the review bot is locked out. The plan gives no rollback, no back-out step and no recovery guidance. If the charset check fails deterministically, re-running only repeats the lockout.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (service-user.sh rotate path)
scenarios: An AWS session token expires between generation and put-parameter: the bot's SSM value is stale while Gerrit has revoked it.
Gerrit's generated password contains a char outside the allowlist: every run deletes the working token and exits 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Preflight `aws sts get-caller-identity` and the template's existence before touching Gerrit. On failure after generation, print 'Gerrit token was rotated but not stored; re-run service-user.sh to rotate again' to stderr, never the token, and exit non-zero. Document the same recovery in infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md.

Add a fixture with indentation, a backslash and no trailing newline that must round-trip byte-for-byte apart from the token.
evidence: "The template render becomes a bash `while read` loop with `${line//__BOT_TOKEN__/$TOKEN}` (no process; the charset check excludes `&` and `\`)."
AC1: "(for example `--value file://` from a pipe, and `ENVIRON` in awk)"
findings.finding: The template render is under-specified as a bash `while read` loop. It omits `IFS= read -r` (without it, leading/trailing whitespace is stripped and backslashes in the template are mangled). It also omits handling a final line with no trailing newline (dropped by a plain `while read`). The plan does address bash 5.2 `patsub_replacement` (`&`) and backslash in the replacement string, via the charset check. The chosen approach also diverges from the AC's own example (`ENVIRON` in awk), which avoids the line-handling pitfalls.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (template render) vs Acceptance Criterion 1
scenarios: The webhooks template has indented YAML/ini or a `\` sequence: the rendered file differs from the template beyond the token substitution.
The template's last line lacks a newline and is silently dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `BOT_TOKEN="$TOKEN" awk '{gsub(/__BOT_TOKEN__/, ENVIRON["BOT_TOKEN"])}1' "$template" > "$out"`. The token travels via env, not argv; the existing charset check already excludes `&`/`\`, which gsub treats specially. Align the Approach text with AC1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure disposition of each post-generation step in service-user.sh (validation failure, SSM put failure, render failure): the resulting Gerrit/SSM/env-file state, and that rerunning the script is the retryable recovery (or reorder steps so nothing destructive precedes validation).
evidence: "deletes the `default` token (as today) and runs `gerrit set-account <bot> --generate-http-password`"
"exits 1 without printing unless the value is non-empty and only `[A-Za-z0-9+/=._~-]`"
No statement of what state remains or how to recover after a post-generation failure.
findings.finding: The rotation path in service-user.sh now runs in this order: delete the 'default' token, generate a new password on the server, capture and validate it, then put it to SSM and render the env file. The plan adds a failure arm ('exits 1 without printing unless the value is non-empty and only [A-Za-z0-9+/=._~-]') but never states the disposition of that arm. At that point Gerrit has already replaced the bot's password and the new value has been discarded unprinted, so the bot is locked out and nothing records the value. The same gap applies if the SSM put fails after Gerrit was updated. The plan does not say whether rerunning is the safe recovery (retryable, regenerates), what state Gerrit, SSM and the env file are left in, or that the three-store update is non-atomic.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (infra/gerrit/service-user.sh)
scenarios: Gerrit's generated password contains a character outside the allowed set, or the output format differs. The script exits 1 after Gerrit has already switched passwords; the review bot gets 401s and the operator has no token to store.

Say that any failure after `--generate-http-password` leaves Gerrit on an unstored password and is recovered by rerunning service-user.sh, which regenerates the password and is idempotent. Have the script print a non-secret message saying so on exit 1, and add a test that a second run after a forced aws failure converges.

findings.finding: git_auth needs a base64 'user:pw' value for `Authorization: Basic ...`, but the plan never says how that encoding is produced. The obvious shell tools wrap their output: GNU `base64` at 76 characters, `openssl base64` at 64. 'rebar-review-bot:' plus a Gerrit-generated password of about 40 characters is near or past the 57-byte input size that produces 76 output characters, and operator passwords from a credential helper can be any length. A wrapped value puts a newline into GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>, so the header is malformed. The no-wrap flags also differ between GNU and BSD/macOS base64, and operator workstations are often macOS.

scenarios: A long operator password or bot token produces wrapped base64, and git push/clone returns 401 or rejects the header.

findings.suggested_fix: In lib-credentials.sh: `b64=$(printf '%s:%s' "$user" "$pw" | base64 | tr -d '\n\r')`. This works with GNU and BSD base64 and keeps the secret on stdin. Add a test where user plus password is at least 80 bytes and assert the GIT_CONFIG_VALUE decodes to the exact credential.

findings.finding: The plan replaces the awk render with 'a bash while read loop with ${line//__BOT_TOKEN__/$TOKEN}', but does not require `IFS= read -r` or handling of a final line with no trailing newline. The committed template uses tab-indented keys (webhooks.config:8-18). A plain `read` strips those tabs, and without -r it mangles backslashes. The rendered file would then differ from what is in refs/meta/config, so `git diff --cached --quiet` would fail and every run would push a whitespace-rewritten webhooks.config. Separately, the substitution path is effectively dead: the template in the same checkout is secret-free and has no __BOT_TOKEN__ (grep finds the placeholder only in service-user.sh), and an older checkout would run its own older script. A simpler, more robust option is to copy the template unchanged and fail if it contains __BOT_TOKEN__. That removes the token from the render entirely and avoids writing the bot token into refs/meta/config.
